$comment: Reviewed, time-boxed exceptions for `npm run audit:ci`.
Every entry needs a reason, the mitigation that makes it acceptable, and a reviewBy date.
The gate fails when an entry expires, when an allowlisted advisory stops appearing
(the exception is stale and must be deleted), or when its severity changes.
See the 'Dependency audit state' section of README.md for the full analysis.

advisories.title: deepmerge mergeObject() allows prototype poisoning of returned objects
advisories.reason: Re-reviewed 2026-11-05; now the only exception, after image-size, @grpc/grpc-js, glob and minimatch were fixed through `overrides`. Build and test tooling only: @react-native-community/cli (and its cli-config, cli-doctor) -> deepmerge@4.3.1, and jest -> @jest/core -> jest-config -> deepmerge. The advisory covers >=4.2.0 <=4.3.1 with no patched version (GitHub lists first_patched_version as null) and 4.3.1 is the latest published release, so there is nothing to override to. npm's fixAvailable is a downgrade of @react-native-community/cli to 11.4.1, which the README's 'Do not run npm audit fix --force' section rules out. Vendoring a hardened copy was considered and declined as not worth maintaining for a low-severity, unreachable flaw.
advisories.mitigation: Never in the shipped app. deepmerge only merges this project's own CLI and Jest configuration objects on a developer machine or CI runner; no user-, network- or device-supplied object ever reaches it, so there is no attacker to supply a __proto__ key.
